s1-001-50e535afcecd3c64.wav.text: The last episode of the transformer series.

s1-002-3019f41fcfb2510b.wav.text: Two topics that both look like implementation details and are not.

s1-003-1b75cabba7e94807.wav.text: Sampling, which is where "the model is bad" usually turns out to mean "the sampler is wrong".

s1-004-168464496fe65e9b.wav.text: And the key-value cache, which is not an optimisation so much as the removal of an obvious mistake.

s10-002-3270024cb897ee86.wav.text: Attention is a differentiable dictionary lookup, and the square root is a variance fix.

s10-003-9361d726336fdf39.wav.text: The block is two writes to a shared residual bus, and the MLP holds two thirds of the parameters.

s10-004-479cd02e5f566a20.wav.text: RoPE falls out of one wish about relative position and is the only scheme that has an answer past the training length.

s10-005-236577e27d1f9597.wav.text: The model learned the grammar of the tape completely and its meaning barely, and our first interpretability experiment measured a positional shortcut rather than the circuit we were looking for.

s10-006-d7743f2f4f214229.wav.text: And the key-value cache removes quadratic waste, at a memory cost that is the whole reason paged caches exist.

s10-007-6290a55282280eee.wav.text: What you have built is the architecture that AlphaSLM, the embedding model, the vision transformer and the speech model in this course are all instances of.

s10-008-dfbef85939c1c2be.wav.text: Next topic, T15: this architecture, plus the tokenizer you built in phase one, plus a real pretraining pipeline.

s2-001-e7d6e283f4405498.wav.text: A trained model hands you a probability for every token in the vocabulary.

s2-002-56c6ce8a3bca75d9.wav.text: Choosing one of them is not part of the model.

s2-003-03873ebd1b898967.wav.text: It is a separate design problem, and it affects perceived quality more than most architecture decisions do.

s2-005-1e4bc45256bda4df.wav.text: Greedy, always take the most likely token: deterministic, and it loops.

s2-006-b274144e0edefb95.wav.text: Temperature, divide the logits before the softmax: below one sharpens, above one flattens, and it never removes an option, only reweights.

s2-007-20baeabf2a1c2312.wav.text: Top-k, keep the k most likely: a fixed budget regardless of how confident the model is.

s2-008-b9030c5105ec752c.wav.text: And top-p, also called nucleus: keep the smallest set of tokens whose probability adds up to p.

s2-009-d4cfc972ba05fffa.wav.text: All four are pure functions of a logit vector, which is worth noticing, because it means you can test them properly instead of squinting at generated text and forming an impression.

s3-000-a248c2ce32eb0e26.wav.text: Here is nucleus sampling in seven lines, with the mistake everyone makes marked.

s3-001-e0ecefa59f5bdcd6.wav.text: Sort descending, take the cumulative probability.

s3-003-4d6549974fa135ee.wav.text: We subtract this token's own probability from the cumulative sum, so what we compare against p is the mass *before* this token.

s3-004-8766fb0f23c4e3f4.wav.text: That means the token which *crosses* the threshold is kept, not dropped.

s3-005-09e509b85d76486a.wav.text: Get that wrong — compare the cumulative sum directly — and you systematically drop the token that was about to complete the nucleus, which quietly makes the model more conservative than you asked for.

s3-006-ef451113ddc74126.wav.text: Line five keeps the argmax alive unconditionally, which is what makes top p of zero point zero one still leave exactly one token rather than none.

s3-007-46152e11582cbce6.wav.text: And line six scatters the mask back into vocabulary order, because a filter that reorders your logits is a filter that samples the wrong token.

s4-000-30be8dcc81b11240.wav.text: And this is the argument for nucleus sampling, on two real rows from one real model.

s4-001-f82da8086da8935e.wav.text: On the left, a confident position: the model has just seen A-L-P-H-A-I-N-F and is ninety nine point eight percent sure the next character is R.

s4-002-ec90397a67c5a434.wav.text: Top-k with k of twenty keeps twenty candidates — nineteen of which the model has already ruled out, every one of them a typo waiting to be drawn.

s4-003-be718982c405cb20.wav.text: Top-p with p of zero point nine keeps one.

s4-004-7af51236a9045f54.wav.text: On the right, an genuinely uncertain position: the model has just emitted a date and is choosing between five ticker symbols, with probabilities zero point three one, zero point two one, zero point one nine, zero point one eight, zero point one.

s4-007-0c07a0b9c05b7004.wav.text: The budget follows the model's own confidence, which is a thing a constant k cannot do, and that is why nucleus sampling is the default in every serving stack you will meet.

s5-000-7f28f8a62d05e06e.wav.text: We swept eleven settings and scored each on two things: how many generated lines match the tape grammar exactly, and how many are distinct.

s5-002-49dfb3c639593309.wav.text: It scores one hundred percent on grammar and twenty five percent on distinctness.

s5-003-6eee49fb94dfa248.wav.text: It produces the same safe line over and over, because the argmax of a language model is not fluent text — it is the least risky token at every step, forever, and least-risky compounds into a loop.

s5-004-63385064744de0cb.wav.text: At the other end, temperature one point five scores zero percent on grammar: variety bought by breaking the structure.

s5-005-4736d62c3bbfe5a8.wav.text: The useful settings sit in the middle, and the two columns together catch both failure modes, which one column alone would not.

s6-001-e254c64609742ba5.wav.text: Think about what generating token t costs without one.

s6-002-aafb791ff571069c.wav.text: You take the whole sequence so far, run it through every layer, and read the logits off the last position.

s6-003-ffdcee5ac3d9c251.wav.text: Next step, you do it again with one more token.

s6-004-8dfeece1a72f091c.wav.text: But the causal mask guarantees that nothing in the past depends on the future, so the keys and values for every position before the newest one are bit-for-bit what they were a moment ago.

s6-006-2a4eff5468a165f0.wav.text: Counted for one hundred and twenty eight generated tokens from an eleven-token prompt: nine thousand five hundred and thirty six position-passes through every layer without a cache, one hundred and thirty nine with one.

s6-007-81e033d74180068a.wav.text: Sixty eight times the work, every bit of it reproducing numbers you already had.

s6-008-e586b701be05584f.wav.text: That is not a missed optimisation.

s6-009-a7f8c7f4ae9a8cf1.wav.text: That is a mistake, and it is quadratic.

s7-000-767bdd02d272abab.wav.text: Measured on two CPU cores, and the shape is the point.

s7-001-9ebd47e488af79c6.wav.text: At thirty two tokens the cache is one point seven times faster.

s7-002-9538036f9df725d3.wav.text: At sixty four, one point nine.

s7-003-2adff722ef13111d.wav.text: At one hundred and twenty eight, two point eight.

s7-005-b48812c700fc82c8.wav.text: The speedup grows with length because the thing being avoided grows with length.

s7-006-668fd3cd8593ac06.wav.text: And at very short lengths a cache can actually lose, because it pays fixed per-step overhead to save arithmetic there is not much of yet.

s7-007-12062d34180c4b2e.wav.text: The output is token-identical at every length under greedy decoding, and there is a test that asserts exactly that — plus a stronger one that compares the *logits*, not just their argmax, because a subtly wrong cache can survive greedy decoding for quite a while before it shows.

s8-000-8b249ef347ec9853.wav.text: One gotcha, and it is specific to the combination of the last two episodes.

s8-001-c5371b4f47d5979a.wav.text: With rotary embeddings, the key is rotated by its position.

s8-002-0a7f567be74860ee.wav.text: A cached key was stored at some earlier position, and it has to carry that rotation with it.

s8-003-d87d86e91ae23d46.wav.text: So you rotate before you write into the cache, never after you read out of it.

s8-004-2abdb18199cfea70.wav.text: Get the order wrong and every cached key is rotated by the *current* position instead of its own, the relative-phase property silently stops holding, and the model is wrong in a way that produces no crash and no obvious garbage.

s8-005-6f8bb459d9a53724.wav.text: Our test for this checks the offset path against a contiguous forward pass, and it is one of the few tests in the repository I would call load-bearing.

s9-000-16eba10a5bccbb57.wav.text: And then the cache runs out, which is the last thing this topic has to teach.

s9-001-0d8ce80341873b4d.wav.text: Ours is the naive version: one preallocated tensor per layer, filled left to right, and when it is full it is full.

s9-002-12e70319593ff97f.wav.text: The size is linear in context times batch times layers times heads times head dimension, times two for keys and values, times four bytes.

s9-003-a21d5ea6dd7de403.wav.text: Here that is one megabyte for a two hundred and fifty six token context on a four layer model, which is nothing.

s9-004-cc4ac53fc4f1ac38.wav.text: For a seven billion parameter model at four thousand tokens of context it is gigabytes — per sequence.

s9-005-6a50b05705d224c5.wav.text: Larger than the model's activations, and mostly empty most of the time, because most requests are shorter than the maximum.

s9-006-20839e5b486e96b2.wav.text: Our generate function raises an error rather than quietly sliding the window, deliberately, so that you meet the wall yourself.

s9-007-e8891eecd3872b7b.wav.text: That wall is the entire motivation for T12, the paged key-value cache, and the design will make a great deal more sense to you having hit it.
